newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Chuan Soon Huat to tap China for Asian growth.
newsitem.headline: Chuan Soon Huat to tap China for Asian growth.

text.p: Singapore's Chuan Soon Huat Industrial Group Ltd (CSH) said on Tuesday it was expanding into China with a new door factory.
The group, which makes and distributes doors, conservatories and joinery products, said at the briefing of its initial public offering, that it was building a factory in Kunshan in China.
It is offering 51.25 million shares at Singapore S$0.35 each to be listed on the main board of the Stock Exchange of Singapore.

On completion of the second phase of its China factory in early 1997, it would be able to produce 500,000 doors annually, initially for the China market, officials said. The first phase was completed in August 1996.
CSH would concentrate on the China market for growth in Asia, after penetrating European and North American markets, said managing director Lee Thian Soon.
"In mid-1996, we set up a new marketing arm in China and we are building up a marketing network in major cities in China," said Geoffrey Aldridge, CSH's executive director.
CSH was aiming to further grow in Europe and North America through new products and by targeting new markets, company officials said.
The group now derives about 42 percent of its turnover from Britain, 33 percent from Europe and 23 percent from North America.
For the eight months ended August 1996, CSH recorded a net profit of S$2.7 million on sales of about S$28 million.

CSH's main production base is in West Java, Indonesia, run by its subsidiary PT Cemerlang Selaras. It has a factory in Singapore that is being expanded and will be used to manufacture steel doors and other products.
"Our strength is that we are close to the source of our materials with our manufacturing base in Indonesia," said Lee.
CSH was also building a second factory in Indonesia, which when completed in mid-1997, would increase the group's capacity by 50 percent, officials said.
Its output from Indonesia is exported to Europe, the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. CSH currently ships an average of 130 containers per month out of Indonesia.
CSH was diversifying into the use of new raw materials such as softwood, medium density fibre board, plywood, veneer and steel, the officials said.
It was also diversifying into furniture trading, renovation and contracting business.
